subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should OpenClaw expand the enforced-plan path for common shell-shaped allowlist matches, or keep the current fail-closed prompt and document it as an intentional limitation?
rationale: The reported behavior contradicts the documented `on-miss` contract, but the current gate protects a security boundary when OpenClaw cannot bind the raw shell command to an enforced execution plan.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin matches
options.body: Support shell-free normalization for clearly enforceable shapes such as tilde-expanded script paths or independently allowlisted simple chains while preserving approval for dynamic or unbound shell constructs.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep the current approval prompt for command shapes that cannot be materialized and update docs plus warning text so operators know to use argv-clean absolute paths for unattended jobs.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell text
options.body: Run all matched Darwin allowlist commands without an enforced plan, accepting a broader shell-resolution risk that current code intentionally avoids.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin matches
recommendation.body: Support shell-free normalization for clearly enforceable shapes such as tilde-expanded script paths or independently allowlisted simple chains while preserving approval for dynamic or unbound shell constructs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest owner from the gateway exec approval gate and authorization-plan history.
